subject: Post-call: model fit & function-calling evals
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@findata.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 16:05:00 -0000
Subject: Post-call: model fit & function-calling evals

Thanks for taking the time earlier, Alex — good conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps: 

Summary from today's discovery:
- Primary use case: structured extraction from semi-structured financial filings + API-first delivery to downstream systems.
- Key constraints: JSON schema compliance for downstream ingesters, deterministic retries behavior (idempotency + clear error codes), and 200–500ms median token latency target for 1–3k QPS.
- Success metrics: >=95% JSON schema passes (strict validation), <=1% malformed outputs that require manual correction, and acceptable latency/cost tradeoff.

What Redwood can run quickly:
- Focused function-calling evals using your schema (we ran a 500-example smoke during the call).
- Larger run: 10k prompt set across edge cases (we'll include the worst-case prompts you flagged).
- Model recommendations: start with redwood-13b-quant (best quality -> structured output stability) and a cost/latency candidate redwood-3b-q for A/B. We'll provide latency/quality curves.

Deliverables / next steps:
1) We'll upload the prompt sets + initial eval summary to the Drive link below and share a short report by EOD Monday. (Attachment: 20261120_prompt_sets.zip, model_eval_results_summary.csv)
2) Marissa/Neha will propose an eval plan for structured-output testing and schema enforcement (see attached redwood_eval_plan.md).
3) We want your canonical JSON schemas for the objects you ingest. If you can attach the current schema, we'll wire it directly into our validator.
4) Schedule a 30-min follow-up demo of our function-calling reliability and how retries/error codes surface in the console.

Questions for you now:
- Can you confirm the example schema file (Sam, can you attach the canonical schema if possible)?
- Are the latency SLOs firm or negotiable for the proof-of-concept run?

Thanks — I’ll coordinate the eval run once we have the schema.

—
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachment: 20261120_prompt_sets.zip (prompt set bundle)
Attachment: model_eval_results_summary.csv (CSV summary of smoke run)

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@findata.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sam Patel <sam.patel@findata.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 16:28:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Post-call: model fit & function-calling evals

Thanks Rishi — good recap. A few clarifying questions before you start the 10k run: 

1) JSON schema compliance: our downstream requires exact key types and no extra-top-level keys. When you say "schema validator", does Redwood run a strict JSON Schema Draft-07+ validator and report failures per-field? Will you also categorize failures (type mismatch vs missing vs extra field)?

2) Retries: Our ingestion pipeline expects the LLM response to be retry-safe. If the model returns partial/invalid JSON, we prefer a deterministic re-ask strategy (fixed number of retries with the same prompt + explicit error codes). Can you confirm Redwood supports retry policies and will include per-example retry counts in the report?

3) Latency SLO: 200–500ms median token latency is what we aim for in production, but for the POC we're flexible if quality requires a higher latency model. Please include latency percentiles for each model variant.

I've attached our canonical schema examples (schema_examples.json) and a small list of problematic filings we want prioritized.

Also — can you include a sample of the raw tokens/response with the validation result for a handful of failure cases? That will help our SREs triage.

Best,
Alex
Product Manager, FinData
alex.johnson@findata.ai

Attachment: schema_examples.json
Attachment: findata_problem_examples.zip

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@findata.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 17:00:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Post-call: model fit & function-calling evals

Great questions, Alex — coupling answers with a proposed plan: 

Schema validation and failure taxonomy:
- We run strict JSON Schema (compatible with Draft-07+) and report per-field failure codes: TYPE_MISMATCH, MISSING_FIELD, EXTRA_FIELD, FORMAT_ERROR. We'll include an aggregated distribution and a per-example failure log.

Retries and deterministic re-asks:
- Redwood Evaluate supports configurable retry policies in the harness: you can set max_retries (e.g., 0–3), backoff style (none, fixed, jitter), and a deterministic re-ask mode that re-sends the same prompt + a short clarifying system message.
- The report will include per-example retry counts, final validation status, and the intermediate responses for failed attempts.

Evaluation plan (high level):
- Stage 1 (3k examples): run on redwood-13b-quant and redwood-3b-q in parallel to get quality/latency curves.
- Stage 2 (10k focused): include long-tail and adversarial prompts from your "problem examples" set.
- Acceptance criteria: >=95% strict schema pass on final responses with <=1% manual correction rate.

Deliverables:
- Eval report (CSV + per-example JSON lines with retry traces).
- Dashboard link with interactive failure filters (see related link).
- Implementation checklist for integration (webhook payloads + error codes).

I attached a short eval plan doc (redwood_eval_plan.md) that lays out timelines and resource needs. With Rishi's confirmation, we can start Stage 1 early next week.

—
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

Attachment: redwood_eval_plan.md

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@findata.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 17:35:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Post-call: model fit & function-calling evals

Adding some reliability/quality-monitoring notes from the eval side: 

1) Regression detection: we'll baseline Stage 1 and configure automatic regression alerts tied to your canonical prompt set. If schema pass-rate drops by >2% vs baseline on any rolling 24h window during the POC, Ops gets paged.

2) Schema drift: we'll run a nightly drift job that reports new keys/field-type shifts and surface examples that introduced the drift.

3) Failure triage: for each failure we'll include the full conversation context, token-level probabilities (where applicable), and a recommended remediation (prompt tweak, model change, or post-processor).

4) Can you confirm whether your downstream ingest supports a tolerant mode (accepting additional fields) during the POC? If yes, we can run an experiment to measure how many extra-field failures would have been tolerated by the ingestor vs strictly rejected.

I'll coordinate the alert thresholds with your SRE once we have samples. Planning note: if you want schema-compliant retries only, we should set max_retries=2 for POC to avoid runaway costs while still recovering simple parser hiccups.

—
Neha Kapoor
Product Lead, Redwood Inference
neha@redwood.ai

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@findata.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 18:10:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Post-call: model fit & function-calling evals

Thanks everyone — that all sounds good. Confirming next steps from FinData: 

- Sam attached the canonical schema (already sent). We'll allow a tolerant mode for the POC (accept additional fields) to help speed iteration, but strict validation is needed for production.
- Please run Stage 1 (3k) on Monday; prioritize the problematic filings list for Stage 2.
- We want the per-example retry traces and token-level snippets for any failing cases.
- Schedule the 30-min demo — Tuesday 10:00am PT works for our team.

If you can send calendar invite, we'll accept. Looking forward to seeing the Stage 1 report.

Best,
Alex
Product Manager, FinData

Attachment: none
